PRIMARY_FINDING.statement: RETRIEVAL_BUDGET_BINDING sets limits.codex = 6 and web_search 3 + web_fetch 3 = 6 retrieval slots. In research_loop.execute() each turn either emits 'final' or retrieves. A model that uses its full, explicitly-stated retrieval allowance therefore consumes all six codex turns and has ZERO turns left in which to produce a report.
PRIMARY_FINDING.root_cause: request_payload() passes 'retrieval_budget' to the model but NEVER passes the codex turn ceiling, and the mechanics string says only 'Return final report when complete'. The model is shown one budget and judged against a second, undisclosed one.
PRIMARY_FINDING.evidence: Attempt 3 ran search/fetch/search/fetch/search/fetch -- exactly 3 and 3, both ceilings hit precisely, six schema-valid actions, zero unapproved tool events -- and was then cut off.
PRIMARY_FINDING.generality: Route-level, not model-level. Any Route D run using full retrieval fails this way on any model, provider path or effort level.
remedies: Raise limits.codex to at least retrieval_slots + 1 (7).
Or disclose the turn ceiling in request_payload so the model can reserve a turn.
PRIMARY_FINDING.status: NOT APPLIED. Both are benchmark METHOD amendments requiring operator authority.

SECONDARY_FINDINGS.detail: cached_input_tokens = 0 with cache_write ~= input on all NINE receipted live turns, which span attempts 1, 2 and 3 (2 + 1 + 6). Route D made TEN live codex turns in total; attempt 1 turn 3 wrote no receipt, and its usage is recorded in evidence/D_DISPATCH_RESULT.json SPEND.turn_03 with cached_input_tokens = 0 as well. Each loop turn is a fresh `codex exec --ephemeral` thread, so the Responses API prompt_cache_key is almost certainly thread-scoped. Roughly 60% of Route D's cost was re-sending an unchanged 233 KB acceptance_schema prefix.

A latent defect in its narration_preface_count return value is recorded, unapplied, in ERRATA/DEFECT-001-narration-preface-count.json. Regression-proven against attempt 1's real turn-3 fixture. SECONDARY_FINDINGS.detail: The codex exec --json event stream carries no model identifier, so served_model='UNKNOWN' is honest and unavoidable. Catalog presence establishes that the account MAY be served gpt-6-astra; it does not attest which backend served any particular request and does not rule out provider-side aliasing or fallback. The earlier claim that it proved 'no silent fallback occurred' was an unsupported inference and is withdrawn -- see ERRATA/ERRATA.md item E2.

The openai-api provider path works: credential resolved from the child environment via env_key with no codex login, --output-schema round-trips, tool isolation holds, broker retrieval works, and ten live turns completed across three attempts (nine of them receipted). The amendment itself is sound.
